summary: Discusses the need to delegate the E.F.F.3.IP6.ARPA reverse DNS zone so reverse lookups work for 6bone addresses, and makes specific recommendations about the process. It is a best current practice document.

plainLanguage.summary: This BCP describes delegation of a reverse-DNS zone for the 6bone's IPv6 test addresses. It proposes that the 6bone operate the service and delegate parts of it to its top-level providers.

questions: why was ip6.int replaced by ip6.arpa
what is the 6bone reverse dns zone
subtitle: A best-practice request to delegate a reverse-DNS zone for 6bone IPv6 addresses.

tldr.problem: The 6bone needed IP6.ARPA reverse lookups for its experimental address space while transitioning from the earlier IP6.INT arrangement.
tldr.mechanism: The memo asks IANA to delegate E.F.F.3.IP6.ARPA to the 6bone, with further delegation to top-level 6bone providers for the 3FFE::/16 space.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3681 is a Best Current Practice. It describes how the 6bone could provide this service and allow it to end with the network's planned phaseout.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 3681 as a Best Current Practice and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The memo describes the 6bone as a temporary experimental network.

sections.title: The 6bone Reverse-Lookup Need
sections.content:
The 6bone provided a network for IPv6 experimentation using address space allocated by RFC 2471. Reverse lookups had been done through IP6.INT, and the memo says users needed to update software to use IP6.ARPA.

The RFC describes the 6bone as having a limited lifetime and says IP6.ARPA reverse-lookup service was needed for the 3FFE::/16 space during the remaining operation period then anticipated.
sections.plainLanguage: The experimental 6bone needed reverse lookups under IP6.ARPA for its address range. The memo addresses how to operate that service while the test network remained active.

sections.title: The Proposed Delegation
sections.content:
After discussion with Regional Internet Registry communities, the memo says it was considered more practical for the 6bone to provide the service itself. This would relieve the registries of the cost while allowing the IP6.ARPA authority to terminate the service when the planned 6bone end date arrived.

The 6bone operational community planned to add registry attributes so holders of top-level 6bone address space could request delegation to their reverse servers.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal has the 6bone run its own reverse-lookup service. Top-level address holders could request delegation to their own reverse servers.

sections.title: Delegating E.F.F.3.IP6.ARPA
sections.content:
The memo requests that IANA delegate the E.F.F.3.IP6.ARPA domain to the 6bone, following instructions to be supplied by the IAB. Names within the zone would be delegated further among top-level 6bone ISPs, called pTLAs.

The internal delegation is to follow the delegation of 6bone 3FFE::/16 address space.
sections.plainLanguage: The request gives the 6bone control of a reverse-DNS branch and lets its top-level providers manage their portions.
